record.original_question: Let G be a finite group, w a multilinear commutator group-word, and p a prime. Suppose that p divides the order |xy| whenever x is a w-value of p′-order in G and y is a w-value in G of order divisible by p. Is it true that then the verbal subgroup w(G) must be p-nilpotent? Without the assumption that w be multilinear, the answer is negative. An affirmative answer has been obtained in several special cases(J. Algebra, 609(2022), 926–936). Y. Contreras Rojas,

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime. A multilinear commutator word (also called an outer commutator word) is a word obtained by nesting commutators using always pairwise distinct variables; formally, $w_1(x)=x$ is multilinear, and if $u(x_1,\dots,x_m)$ and $v(y_1,\dots,y_n)$ are multilinear commutator words on disjoint sets of variables, then $[u,v]$ is a multilinear commutator word. For a word $w(x_1,\dots,x_n)$, a $w$-value in $G$ is any element of the form $w(g_1,\dots,g_n)^{\pm 1}$ with $g_i\in G$, and the verbal subgroup $w(G)$ is the subgroup generated by all $w$-values. An element of $G$ has $p'$-order if its order is coprime to $p$.

Suppose that $w$ is a multilinear commutator word and that the following condition holds in $G$: for every $w$-value $x\in G$ of $p'$-order and every $w$-value $y\in G$ whose order is divisible by $p$, the prime $p$ divides the order of the product $xy$.

Question: Must the verbal subgroup $w(G)$ be $p$-nilpotent (i.e., must $w(G)$ have a normal Hall $p'$-subgroup)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem with affirmative answers established only in special cases (e.g., for lower central words $\gamma_k$ in general finite groups, and for derived words $\delta_k$ in soluble groups, as in the 2022 paper in J. Algebra 609). No general resolution for arbitrary multilinear commutator words appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: p-nilpotency criteria for some verbal subgroups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies condition P(w,p): p divides |xy| for every w-value x of p'-order and every w-value y of order divisible by p. Proves p-nilpotency of γ_k(G) and (in soluble case) δ_k(G).
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer is known only in special cases (lower central and, in soluble groups, derived words).
